violated_contract: A supervisor that promises callers a best-effort, never-throwing bridge to an optional helper process must intercept every failure channel of the launch API it wraps. Node's spawn reports launch failure on two channels — an asynchronous 'error' event (ENOENT) and a synchronous throw (ENOTDIR through an app.asar path, EACCES) — and handling only the asynchronous channel lets the synchronous one escape the bridge's no-throw contract; launched from a bare startup timer, that escape is a process-fatal uncaughtException that left a window-less zombie holding the single-instance lock. Compounding it, spawn failure was the implicit platform detector: a platform-scoped helper must be gated on process.platform by its owning bridge so unsupported platforms never reach the launch API at all.
canonical_prevention: Route every launch-failure channel into the bridge's single fail-open latch: guard the platform at the top of ensureStarted, wrap the spawn call in try/catch feeding the same 'unavailable' latch (and one-shot fallback record) as the async 'error' path, and prove both with regression tests asserting warm() and all calls stay silent no-ops — no throw, no respawn loop, no fallback noise for by-design platform absence. Sibling helper bridges copying this supervisor shape (automation, OCR) inherit the same contract.
